status: proposed: three options for the Script critic and the Arbiter to choose between. Nothing here is a bible yet.

scope.path: e01, e02 shared; one choice at the end of e02; then a03-a05 or b03-b05. Five episodes on any path, eight to produce, two glimpses.
scope.episode_length: about two minutes (110-140 spoken seconds, 25-40 lines)
scope.production_limits: stills with camera moves, no image-to-video; 4-6 principals with distinct silhouettes; about 5-7 recurring locations; no crowd-dependent beats; action as single strong images
scope.content_notes: Fictional police forces, agencies and insignia; no national flag; no real people; every character is an adult; violence and one suicide are backstory, spoken of or told through objects, never shown.
scope.language_convention: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script in the same line; spoken forms (ये, वो).

not_reused: The Billionaire's Secret, The Last Local and The Wedding Tape (concept note)
ग़लत Bag (photoreal proof scene): none of the three uses its characters or premise

loglines.flavour: Small-town gothic noir: an imposter con wrapped round a buried crime.
loglines.setting: A crumbling haveli and its mango orchard at the edge of a fictional qasba in central UP, in January fog.

logline.en: The night before a court is due to declare her missing husband dead, a man with his scar and his limp walks into the haveli, and the whole family weeps with joy. Only Vasudha knows he is a fraud, and she can never say how she knows: she put the real Dev in the orchard well seven years ago.
logline.hi: जिस रात के अगले दिन देव को कानूनन मृत घोषित होना था, उसी रात वो लौट आया। पूरा घर रो पड़ा। सिर्फ़ वसुधा जानती है कि ये देव नहीं है, क्योंकि असली देव को सात साल पहले उसी ने कुएँ में छुपाया था।

loglines.lead: Vasudha, 38. Has run the haveli, the orchard and her mother-in-law's medicines alone for seven years. Dev came home drunk one foggy night to sell the orchard out from under them; the fight ended on the stone lip of the well, and she hid what happened. Nobody has ever asked her.

hook_e01.first_5_seconds: Diya light. An old woman's fingers read a bearded stranger's face: 'देवू...?' Cut to Vasudha in the doorway as a steel thali slides out of her hands. Everyone in the frame is crying with joy except the wife.
hook_e01.episode: It is the night before the tehsil hearing that will declare Dev dead and divide the land. 'Dev' arrives with the right split eyebrow, the right limp and Vasudha's pet name. Amma, nearly blind, accepts him by touch. Brother-in-law Girish, hours away from his share of the orchard, calls him a fraud. Vasudha says nothing at all.
hook_e01.cliffhanger: Past midnight she carries a lantern to the sealed dry well in the orchard, lays her palm on the slab and whispers: 'तुम तो यहीं हो, देव। तो घर में कौन सो रहा है?'
hook_e01.open_question: Who is the man in the house, and what can a wife do when she cannot say how she knows?

loglines.e02_to_choice: The man passes every test Girish sets: where Dev hid his bottles, the song he sang to their daughter Gauri. He lets Vasudha see that he is watching her, not the family. Alone, she opens a spice tin and looks at a broken glass bangle and a torn corner of the land deed: that night, told in two objects. Next morning in the SDM's chamber the hearing becomes an identification. Amma says yes, Girish says no, and the officer rules that the wife's word decides. He asks her one question: 'ये आपके पति हैं?'

choice.asked_at: End of e02, in the SDM's chamber, with every other character looking at her.

question.hi: इसे अपना पति कह दूँ, या झूठा?
question.en: Do I call him my husband, or a liar?

A.does: She identifies the stranger as Dev.
A.gain: A living Dev was never killed: the well is safe for good. Girish's claim dies in that room, and Amma has her son back.
A.cost: On her own sworn word she hands a stranger a husband's rights over her house, the land and her daughter's inheritance. She can never take it back without admitting she lied to a court.

B.gain: The stranger is out of her house and her room, and her word is still her own.
B.cost: Amma loses her son a second time, by Vasudha's mouth. The declaration goes ahead, so Girish gets his claim on the orchard. And the question nobody has asked in seven years is asked in front of an officer: if this is not Dev, where is he, and why is she so sure?

choice.why_hard: The viewer knows what the family does not. Saying yes buries her crime for ever and lets a predator into her room with the law on his side. Saying no throws him out, hands Girish the orchard and starts the one inquiry she cannot survive. A protective viewer says yes; a proud or honest one says no; neither is safe.

loglines.cost_each_way: Yes: she gives a stranger legal power over her home, her land and her daughter's inheritance, on a lie she can never withdraw. No: she breaks Amma's heart again, lets Girish take his share of the orchard, and invites the question of where the real Dev is.

branches.A: Marriage of lies. Legally her husband, the man moves into her room and starts selling the orchard. Then he tells her why he was sure she would say yes: he was in the orchard that night, come to collect Dev's gambling debt, and he watched her at the well. Two people who can hang each other share one house, and Vasudha has to learn to run a con of her own.
branches.B: The net. The man is led away saying she should be asked how she can be so certain. The daroga who closed the missing-person file seven years ago reopens it. Girish bails the imposter out to help him look for a body, Gauri starts asking what happened the night her father left, and the spades get closer to the well.

endings.A: She turns his stolen name into his cage: as Dev he cannot accuse her of killing Dev, and as Dev he inherits Dev's old warrant and debts. He signs the orchard over to Gauri and leaves in the fog. The secret holds, and Vasudha relights Amma's diya as the best liar in the house.
endings.B: Before Girish's hired spades reach the well, Vasudha tells Gauri and Amma herself. Amma answers that she heard the fight that night and chose for seven years not to know. Vasudha walks the daroga to the well and blows out the seven-year diya: the secret is over, the orchard is someone else's fight, and her daughter is holding her hand.

A.shows: The night after the hearing. The man sits down on Dev's side of the bed and unlaces his shoes: 'अब तो तुमने ख़ुद कह दिया, वसुधा।' Her hand closes round the door bolt.
A.ends_on: Without turning round, he asks: 'बाग़ वाला कुआँ कब से बंद है?'
A.must_not_reveal: That he was in the orchard that night; how she gets rid of him.

B.shows: The man is walked out of the chamber by a constable. At the door he stops and says to the daroga, smiling at Vasudha: 'इनसे पूछिए, इन्हें इतना यक़ीन कैसे है।'
B.ends_on: The daroga's pen stops moving. His eyes go to her.
B.must_not_reveal: That Amma half-knew; that Vasudha confesses.

principal_cast.silhouette: 38. Faded indigo cotton saree, low bun, thin mangalsutra, a pale scar at the hairline. Upright, economical in every movement.
About 43. Gaunt, grey-shot beard, rust-brown shawl, split left eyebrow, a limp and a walking stick.
70. White saree, clouded eyes, rudraksha beads, hands always reaching for a face or a wall.
36. Thick moustache, tight checked shirt, gold ring, a motorbike key hooked on one finger.
19. Jeans and a short kurta, college backpack, long single braid.

principal_cast.role: supporting; can be held to three scenes
principal_cast.silhouette: 52. Khaki with invented insignia, wool muffler, paunch, slow eyes.

locations: Haveli courtyard with the tulsi platform and the diya niche
Vasudha's bedroom: a double bed with one side unused for seven years
Mango orchard and its sealed dry well
The SDM's chamber at the tehsil office
Haveli gate and lane in fog
loglines.production_fit: Six people, six places, no crowds: the village is fog and voices beyond the gate. Nearly every beat is a face, a hand or an object (diya, well slab, door bolt, thumbprint, broken bangle). Night scenes are lit by lantern and diya, which suits photoreal stills and hides background drift. The ballot is a single yes or no.
risks: Six principals is the top of the limit; the daroga is written to be cut down if needed.

A missing person who returns is in the same family as The Last Local in the concept note (a daughter missing twelve years). The engine here is different (an imposter con and a guilty wife), but the Arbiter should judge whether it is far enough away.
A small-town setting and a khaki daroga sit near Series 2's world. Tone and look are opposite, but the two series would share a milieu.
The seven-year presumption of death is Indian law as I recall it, and the identification hearing is dramatised. Neither was checked against a source in this session.
Slowest burn of the three: it depends on performance and silence more than on incident.

loglines.flavour: Con-artist chamber thriller, with a slow-burning attraction that may be a trap.
loglines.setting: A newly-wed's bedroom in a rented house in a small Madhya Pradesh city, over one long night; then a highway and a marriage bureau.

logline.en: Kiran has married eight men and vanished with the jewellery before each sunrise. On her ninth wedding night the groom opens his eyes and tells her to pour in the whole sachet. He has spent fourteen months making himself her mark, because the sixth husband her gang robbed was his little brother, who was found hanging eleven days later. He wants the woman who runs the brides. He does not know the bride he is hunting is sitting on his bed.
logline.hi: आठ शादियाँ, और आठ बार सुबह से पहले गहने लेकर ग़ायब। नौवीं रात दूल्हे ने आँखें खोलीं और कहा: 'पूरी पुड़िया डाल दो।' उसे वो औरत चाहिए जो ये दुल्हनें भेजती है, और वो दुल्हन जिसने उसके भाई को लूटा था। उसे नहीं पता कि वो दुल्हन उसी के सामने बैठी है।

loglines.lead: Kiran, 27, tonight 'Sneha'. Raised from fourteen by Shakun Mausi, whose marriage bureau supplies brides who disappear. Mausi has promised this is her last wedding and is holding her ₹18 lakh share. A burn scar on her left wrist sits hidden under the bridal chooda.

hook_e01.first_5_seconds: Extreme close-up: hennaed fingers tap white powder from a paper fold into a steel glass of kesar milk. Off screen the groom, eyes shut on a bed strewn with marigolds: 'पूरी पुड़िया डाल दो। आधी में मुझे नींद नहीं आती।' Her hand stops.
hook_e01.episode: Aditya, a quiet pharmacist, has padlocked the door from inside and hung the key round his neck. The jewellery in the almirah is brass, the house is rented by the month, and the SIM is gone from her phone. He lays out what he knows about the gang calmly, like a man who has rehearsed it for a year.
hook_e01.cliffhanger: He holds up the one photograph the gang's photographer missed: a veiled bride's hand on his brother Mohit's, a burn scar on the wrist. 'मोहित ग्यारह दिन बाद पंखे से लटका मिला। मुझे ये हाथ चाहिए।' Close on Kiran's left hand, sliding her chooda down over the same scar. He has not seen it yet.
hook_e01.open_question: How long before he sees her wrist, and what does he do when he does?

loglines.e02_to_choice: She never knew Mohit died, and it lands. Aditya's offer: he is not police and he does not want her; lead him to Mausi and she walks away. Her fallback is Billu, the 'brother', parked in the lane until the 3 am signal. A pinned message on her phone shows the viewer the gang's code: 'दूध पी लिया' means all clear, bring the car; 'दूध फट गया' means it is a trap, send the boys. At 2 am Mausi rings for the usual mother's check-in. Aditya puts the call on speaker; he does not know the code. Mausi, warm as ever: 'दामाद जी ने दूध पी लिया, बेटा?'

choice.asked_at: End of e02, on the open phone line, with Aditya watching her mouth.

question.hi: मौसी को इसके हवाले करूँ, या इसे मौसी के?
question.en: Do I hand Mausi to him, or him to Mausi?

A.does: She gives the all-clear, so Billu will drive the two of them straight to Mausi's door.
A.gain: A way out of the life, and a chance to pay something back to the family she broke.
A.cost: The only mother she has had since fourteen, the ₹18 lakh Mausi is holding for her, and the other girls' freedom. And every hour beside Aditya brings him closer to the scar under her bangles.

B.does: She gives the alarm, and Mausi's boys come for Aditya.
B.gain: Her family, her money and her secret: Mausi makes the problem go away and Kiran keeps her promised exit.
B.cost: A second brother from the same family destroyed by her, this time knowingly. The only person who ever offered her a door out is handed to people who will not stop at robbing him.

choice.why_hard: Mausi exploits her and loves her, and the shared episodes show both. Aditya is wronged and frightening, and his justice ends at Kiran's own wrist. Loyalty and self-preservation pull one way, guilt and the wish to get out pull the other, and helping the right man is the choice most likely to destroy her.

loglines.cost_each_way: All-clear: she loses Mausi, her ₹18 lakh and the other girls, and walks beside a man who is hunting the scar on her own wrist. Alarm: she knowingly destroys a second brother and closes the only door out of the life.

branches.A: Road and sting. Kiran walks Aditya into the bureau as her greedy new husband who wants a cut. In the next room Chhoti, nineteen, is being dressed for her first wedding. Aditya gets within reach of Mausi's ledger, and within reach of Kiran's wrist.
branches.B: Hostage and coup. Billu and the boys take the house. Mausi arrives in person, tender and practical, and Kiran learns two things: what 'handling him' means, and that her ₹18 lakh was never going to be paid. To keep a man alive she has to con the woman who taught her how.

endings.A: Mausi is taken with her own ledger. Kiran slides off the chooda and shows Aditya the scar herself; he steps back and lets the police have her. At the station she gives her real name for the first time in thirteen years.
endings.B: Kiran turns the boys against Mausi and lets Aditya go at dawn, alive and with nothing to show for it. Last image: her hennaed hand steadying Chhoti's over a glass of milk. She is the new Mausi.

A.shows: Dawn, Billu's car. Aditya in the back seat playing the greedy husband, Kiran in front. Billu, without turning: 'जीजाजी को मौसी से मिलना है? मौसी किसी से नहीं मिलतीं।'
A.ends_on: The car stops at the bureau's shutter. Aditya reaches forward to help Kiran out and takes her left hand, the bangle hand.
A.must_not_reveal: Whether he sees the scar; what happens to Mausi; that Kiran gives herself up.

B.shows: Headlights swing across the bedroom ceiling. Boots on the stairs. Aditya looks at Kiran: 'तुमने उससे क्या कहा?'
B.ends_on: The padlock he fixed on the inside is broken from the outside, and Mausi's voice comes through the door: 'दरवाज़ा खोलिए, दामाद जी।'
B.must_not_reveal: What Mausi intends for him; that Kiran takes over.

principal_cast.silhouette: 27. Plain red saree, red-and-ivory chooda to mid-forearm, old-style henna (a solid disc on each palm and dipped fingertips, no fine pattern to drift), small nose ring. After the first night: the same chooda with a grey salwar-kurta.
33. Tall and narrow, cream wedding kurta, rimless glasses, careful pharmacist's hands, a brass key on a red thread round his neck.
56. Broad, starched green cotton saree, large maroon bindi, a bunch of keys at the waist, paan-stained smile.
30. Wiry, denim jacket, gelled hair, car key and a toothpick.
19. Slight, long braid, half-finished henna, a phone always in her hand.

locations: The bridal bedroom: marigold strings, steel almirah, padlocked door, one window on the lane
The house's stairwell and front door
The lane at night with Billu's parked car
The car interior on an empty highway at dawn
Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau and Beauty Parlour: mirror wall, bridal mannequin, steel cashbox
A small police chowki desk, fictional force (branch A only)
loglines.production_fit: Both shared episodes are two people in one locked room: the most controllable set of the three, built from the images stills do best (glass, padlock, key, wrist, phone screen). The ballot can show the two spoken phrases as the options. Five principals, six places, and no crowd: the wedding is over when we arrive.
risks: Four minutes in one room lives or dies on the dialogue. The critic should hold the two-hander to a high bar.
Bridal detail is the main consistency risk. The design avoids it: plain saree, no heavy jewellery, block-style henna, and the chooda as the one fixed marker.
The vote could tilt to A (helping the wronged man). Aditya has to be written as a real threat to her and Mausi's care as real, or it will not split.
Runaway-bride gangs are a familiar news story in India and have been used on screen before; the new turn is that the groom is the trap. I did not check for a close existing match.
Mohit's death is spoken of, never shown.

loglines.flavour: Cyber-con thriller: darkly funny for thirty seconds, then a moral vice.
loglines.setting: A rented flat on the edge of the NCR, one wall dressed as a police station for video calls, and a doctor's study in Lucknow seen through his webcam.

logline.en: Kabir failed the police exam three times. Now he wears a fake uniform on video calls and 'digitally arrests' frightened people until they pay. Tonight's target, a respected doctor, is told 'we know everything' and breaks down: he confesses to hiding the body of his wife, missing for three years. A fake cop now holds a real confession, a boss who smells crores, and a daughter who thinks he is the first officer who ever cared.
logline.hi: तीन बार police भर्ती में fail हुआ कबीर अब नकली वर्दी पहनकर video call पर लोगों को 'digital arrest' करता है। आज रात एक doctor डरकर वो क़बूल कर बैठा जो किसी ने पूछा ही नहीं था: तीन साल से लापता बीवी की मौत।

loglines.lead: Kabir Solanki, 24. Three failed attempts at the sub-inspector exam, a father who mortgaged three bighas to pay for his coaching, and a gift for sounding like the law. On calls he is 'Inspector Vikram Rathore'.

hook_e01.first_5_seconds: Tight on a stern young officer, khaki collar, a crest on the wall behind him: 'आप digital arrest में हैं। Camera बंद मत कीजिए।' Cut wide: under the desk he is in shorts and rubber chappals, and the police station is a flex banner taped to a bedroom wall, a ring light, and a pressure cooker whistling next door.
hook_e01.episode: The routine: Zoya plays the senior madam, Rana listens on an earbud and prompts. The night's target is Dr Avinash Bhalla, 61, alone in his study, told that his identity is tied to a laundering case and that he may not leave the camera's sight. Kabir pushes the standard line: 'हमें सब पता है। ख़ुद बता देंगे तो मदद होगी।'
hook_e01.cliffhanger: The doctor takes off his glasses and starts to cry: 'वो accident था। नीलम सीढ़ियों से गिरी थी... मैंने उसे सिर्फ़ छुपाया।' Kabir looks down at his script. There is no line for this. The recording light is on.
hook_e01.open_question: Who is Neelam, and what does a fake policeman do with a real confession?

loglines.e02_to_choice: Kabir mutes and searches: Neelam Bhalla, missing three years; her daughter Ira still posts appeals. Rana is delighted: this is not a twelve-lakh mark, it is a cash machine. The doctor, still sure they are police, offers two crore to settle it quietly. Zoya begs Kabir to take it: no court will believe scammers, so this is the only punishment the man will ever get. Then Ira walks into the study with her father's tea and sees a uniform on the screen. The doctor panics: 'ये... मम्मी के case के सिलसिले में हैं।' Three years of nothing, and now an officer. She leans into the camera: 'Sir, कुछ पता चला?' In Kabir's ear, Rana: 'बोल, कुछ नहीं मिला।'

choice.asked_at: End of e02, on the live video call, with Ira waiting for his answer and Rana in his ear.

question.hi: इसकी बेटी को सच बताऊँ, या दो करोड़ लेकर चुप रहूँ?
question.en: Tell her the truth, or take the two crore?

A.does: He lies to Ira and keeps the doctor on the hook.
A.gain: Two crore. Kabir's share buys back his father's land and gets Zoya out, and Rana stays friendly.
A.cost: Ira goes on searching for a mother he knows is dead. A man who hid a body stays free because Kabir was paid. The uniform stops being a costume: he is a corrupt cop without ever having been a real one.

B.does: He tells Ira, on camera, in front of her father.
B.gain: A daughter learns what happened to her mother, and for one sentence he is the officer he wanted to be.
B.cost: The money is gone and the scam is blown. Rana holds copies of his and Zoya's IDs and their home addresses. The recording that proves the confession also shows Kabir's face in a fake uniform, so prison is likely for both of them, and the confession may not even hold up.

choice.why_hard: Zoya's argument is a good one: if the confession is worthless and they go to jail for nothing, taking everything the doctor owns is the only justice on offer. Against that is one face on a screen asking a direct question. Money, safety and a rough kind of punishment on one side; the truth, at the price of his freedom and Zoya's, on the other.

loglines.cost_each_way: Lie and take the money: Ira never learns the truth, the doctor stays free, and Kabir becomes the corrupt cop he was only pretending to be. Tell her: two crore gone, the scam blown, Rana after him and Zoya, and prison likely for a confession that may not stand.

branches.A: Blackmail noir. The doctor pays the first instalment and then starts asking careful questions of his own; a man who hid one body is not a soft target. Rana wants to milk him for years. And Ira now has Inspector Vikram's number and keeps calling the only policeman who was ever kind to her.
branches.B: Run and reckoning. The doctor kills the call and Rana locks the flat down. Kabir and Zoya get out with the recording on a pen drive and nothing else. Ira tracks the officer down and finds a fraud. The confession is useless without Neelam, and the only people who can help her find her mother are the two scammers who lied to her.

endings.A: Kabir gives the doctor Rana's real name, lets the two of them destroy each other, and goes home with the money. His father garlands 'our officer' beside the redeemed land papers. The phone lights up with Ira's 'Sir, कोई update?' and he turns it face down.
endings.B: They find Neelam in the sealed basement of the nursing home's unfinished wing. Kabir walks into a real police station in the fake uniform and puts the pen drive and his cap on the desk. Ira can hold her mother's last rites; Inspector Vikram's only real arrest is his own.

A.shows: A bank alert on Kabir's phone: fifty lakh credited. Zoya laughing and crying at once. Then the doctor back on the call, calm now, glasses on.
A.ends_on: The doctor: 'Inspector साहब, आपका badge number क्या था?' Kabir says nothing.
A.must_not_reveal: Who ends up with the money; what happens to Rana; Ira's last message.

B.shows: Kabir says it. Ira's face. The doctor's hand slams the laptop shut: black. In the flat, Rana takes out his earbud very slowly and bolts the front door from inside.
B.must_not_reveal: That they get out; the basement; the surrender.

principal_cast.silhouette: 24. Lean, a thin moustache grown for the part, khaki uniform shirt with an invented crest over grey shorts and blue rubber chappals. Outside the flat: the same shirt under a hoodie.
26. Navy blazer over a printed kurta, call-centre headset, bun held with a claw clip, chipped red nail polish.
46. Thickset, maroon tracksuit, gold chain, one white earbud, vape.
61. Silver side-parted hair, cream shawl over a sweater-vest, reading glasses on a cord.
28. Cropped hair, oversized mustard sweater, her mother's small diamond nose pin.

locations: The flat's police-station wall and desk, as the victim's screen shows it
The same room from behind: mattresses, ring light, extension boards, kitchen door
The flat's stairwell and terrace at night
Dr Bhalla's study, as his webcam sees it
The nursing home's unfinished basement (branch B)
A real police station desk, fictional force (branch B); Kabir's village courtyard (branch A)
loglines.production_fit: A video call is the one kind of scene where a held still looks natural. Webcam shots can be full-frame stills with the call interface added in the edit, so faces stay on-model and no screen has to be faked inside an image. Five principals with very different outlines, and no crowds.
risks: The vote may lean to the truth; my guess is 55 to 60 per cent. Zoya's stake and her argument have to land in e02 to pull it back.
The lead starts as a predator. The failed-exam backstory and the comic opening have to buy sympathy inside the first minute.
Needs invented agency names, crests and uniforms for both the fake and the real police. The con is shown as drama, not as a method.
Fake police here and a cop caper in Series 2: both series would lean on khaki.
Digital-arrest scams have been widely covered in India. I did not check whether a film or series already uses the turn where a fake cop gets a real confession.
Whether such a confession is admissible is something a character asserts; it was not checked.
Seven places counting one per ending: the top of the location limit.

showrunner_view.note: Opinion, for the critic and the Arbiter to weigh. The decision and its reasoning belong in docs/decisions.md.
showrunner_view.why: s1-l1 has the cleanest one-sentence premise and the most even choice: the ballot is a single word, and the safe answer and the honest answer both hurt. s1-l2 has the strongest first five seconds and the lowest production risk. s1-l3 is the most topical, but its choice is the likeliest to split unevenly.
showrunner_view.what_would_change_it: Take s1-l2 if the Gate 0 proof shows drift on elderly or bearded faces or on foggy night exteriors, if six principals is judged one too many, or if the Arbiter wants the two series as far apart as possible (s1-l1 shares a small-town milieu with Series 2).
